title: Surviving spouse and inherited IRA - federal options
facts: A surviving spouse generally has special federal options for an inherited IRA that are not available to most nonspouse beneficiaries.
Depending on circumstances, a spouse may be able to treat an inherited IRA as their own, roll eligible assets into their own IRA or retirement plan, or remain a beneficiary of an inherited account.
The best available option can affect required minimum distributions, early-distribution rules and timing, so age and the deceased spouse's RMD status matter.
Nonspouse beneficiaries generally cannot make a spousal-style rollover treating the inherited IRA as their own.
